data.name: Woodman
data.long_meaning: A name of Old English origin, 'Wudmann' or 'Wodhmann', derived from the Old English words 'wudu' meaning 'wood' and 'mann' meaning 'man'. This name was used to describe someone who lived or worked in the woods, possibly as a hunter or woodcutter.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of connection to nature and the natural world.
data.numerology_meaning: Persons with this name have a deep inner sense of justice, and a strong sense of right and wrong. They are individualists who are difficult to influence. They are normally loyal, stable, solid, and practical.

data.cultural_impact: The Christian name "Woodman" resonates with a deep connection to nature and the natural world. Historically, those with this name would have been associated with the woods as hunters, woodcutters, or herdsmen. In contemporary times, a Woodman might be seen as an individual who appreciates and enjoys spending time in nature, allowing for a strong sense of groundedness, independence, and self-sufficiency.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian belief, the name "Woodman" is not only a reminder of our connection to God's natural world but also an invitation to meditate on the biblical figures who lived and worked in the woods. One such figure is St. Francis of Assisi, the patron saint of ecology, who devoted his life to living in harmony with nature as an embodiment of the Gospel message. The name "Woodman" encourages us to live out our faith by recognizing and preserving the natural world as a gift from God.
